claims.text: Additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi exhibits residual thermal stresses.
Additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi exhibits compositional segregation.
Additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi contains processing-induced microstructural defects.
Post-fabrication homogenization heat treatment will relax residual stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Post-fabrication homogenization heat treatment will reduce compositional segregation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Post-fabrication homogenization heat treatment will heal or close processing-induced defects.
The treatment will reduce dislocation density.
Homogenization heat treatment promotes atomic diffusion.
Heat-treatment-driven atomic diffusion relaxes residual stress and homogenizes segregated regions.
Optional cold rolling refines the microstructure.
Reduced residual stresses, segregation, and defects improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
Treated AlCrFeNiSi will have greater tensile strength than untreated additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Treated AlCrFeNiSi will have greater ductility than untreated additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Treated AlCrFeNiSi will have lower residual stress than untreated additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Treated AlCrFeNiSi will have a more homogeneous elemental distribution than untreated additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The intervention is effective when annealing is conducted at approximately 800–1000 °C for 1–4 hours in an inert atmosphere.
The efficacy may vary substantially with additive-manufacturing parameters and feedstock quality.
The magnitude of improvement and the optimal processing parameters are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The initial state calls the AlCrFeNiSi powder itself 'produced via additive manufacturing,' whereas the other fields treat powder as feedstock and additive manufacturing as the operation that produces the samples or builds. This makes the processing sequence internally inconsistent.
